'''Matthew Peter Headrick''' (born ca. 1973<ref name=":0"/>) is an American physicist who is a Professor of [[Physics]] at [[Brandeis University]].<ref name=externalbio>{{cite web|url=http://people.brandeis.edu/~headrick/HeadrickCV.pdf|title=Official Bio}}</ref><ref name=officialsite>{{cite web|url=https://www.brandeis.edu/departments/physics/people/faculty/headrick.html|title=Official Site}}</ref><ref name=cite1/> He received his PhD from [[Harvard University]] in 2002 under [[Shiraz Minwalla]] and his A.B from [[Princeton University]] in 1994.<ref name=officialsite/> Headrick is known for his contributions to the quantum information perspective on holography.

Headrick is notable as the 1990 winner of the [[Intel Science Talent Search|Intel (then Westinghouse) Science Talent Search]] while a high school student at the [[University of Chicago Laboratory Schools]], an event that generated intense media coverage.<ref name=nyt>{{Cite news|title = EDUCATION; From Nitrogen Fixation To a $20,000 Scholarship|url = https://www.nytimes.com/1990/03/07/us/education-from-nitrogen-fixation-to-a-20000-scholarship.html|newspaper = The New York Times|date = 1990-03-07|access-date = 2015-10-29|issn = 0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = All Students Need State-of-the-art Science Education|url = https://www.chicagotribune.com/1990/03/23/all-students-need-state-of-the-art-science-education/|website = tribunedigital-chicagotribune|access-date = 2015-10-29}}</ref> He appeared on talk shows including ''[[Today (American TV program)|Today]]''.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|url = http://www.nbcuniversalarchives.com/nbcuni/clip/5112674437_s23.do|title = Westinghouse Science Project Winners Discuss Their Project (audiovisual file)|last = Gumbel|first = Bryant|date = March 7, 1990|work = NBC News Today Show|location = Today New York Studio|access-date = 2015-10-30|archive-date = 2016-01-05|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160105035833/http://www.nbcuniversalarchives.com/nbcuni/clip/5112674437_s23.do}}</ref> In response to the award, [[James R. Thompson|then-Illinois Gov. Thompson]] declared a "Matthew Headrick Day"<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title = Students Hail The Conquering Scientist|url = https://www.chicagotribune.com/1990/03/10/students-hail-the-conquering-scientist/|website = tribunedigital-chicagotribune|access-date = 2015-10-29}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = Illinois Register|issue=45|date= November 9, 1990|volume=14|page=106|url = http://www.mocavo.com/Illinois-Register-14-Issue-45-November-9-1990-Volume-14/680660/106|website = Mocavo|access-date = 2015-10-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160105050852/https://www.mocavo.com/Illinois-Register-14-Issue-45-November-9-1990-Volume-14/680660/106 |archive-date=5 January 2016}}</ref> and the [[United States House of Representatives|US House of Representatives]] also made a proclamation.<ref name=":0" />
